findings: Claude Code's MCP client: protocolVersion 2025-11-25, capabilities roots + elicitation; after initialize it asks tools/list, prompts/list and resources/list (logs/wire/claude_single_attempt2_auth.jsonl).
For an ok result Claude Code gave the model structuredContent (compact JSON, no spaces); for an isError result it gave the text block. Either way only the tool's returned JSON reached the model.

Claude knows nothing about Northbridge beyond the server's one-line instructions: on the order it looked up the supplier, item, stock, certificate and cost centres itself (8 calls) and asked which Voltway and which date; our harness's system prompt already names BAT-500, VC-EIN-0042 and PRD-07, so it made 4 calls.

With the same two user turns, our harness submitted the request (PR/2026/04417, waiting for Daniel); Claude Code previewed it and asked again. With a third turn ('Yes, submit the purchase request.') it submitted the same request.
Both harnesses tried a direct order first, got the £50,000 limit error from the tool, and recovered by raising a purchase request: the error contract's next_step did the steering.

On the hands prompt (no codes), both harnesses discover the codes. Ours: find_item, find_supplier, check_budget, check_budget(PRD-07), search_policy x2, check_stock, a request preview with a guessed need-by date (2027-02-01, logged as a model error), supplier_certificates; then a second preview and the commit. Claude Code: find_item + find_supplier, supplier_certificates + check_stock, check_budget, preview + check_budget(PRD-07), commit; it never called search_policy. Both end with PR/2026/04417 waiting for Daniel.

The '£273,600 (ex. VAT)' slip was seen once, in our harness's first order run (the app's prompt); it did not recur on the hands prompt or in any Claude Code reply. It is logged in our_harness.json (order.observed_model_errors): the tool's estimated_value includes VAT.

order_on_the_hands_prompt.why: harness.AGENT names BAT-500, VC-EIN-0042, PRD-07 and the 9 Nov date, so our harness skipped the look-ups; l4_prompts.HANDS_L4 keeps the identity, date and rules and drops every code. Same three user turns on both; Claude Code gets HANDS_L4 appended to its own system prompt (--append-system-prompt).
